title: Reading Practice 10 - Artificial Intelligence Ethics
description: IELTS Academic Reading practice about ethical challenges and concerns around AI development.

stimuli.title: Passage 1: Artificial Intelligence Ethics
stimuli.content:
A Artificial intelligence has progressed from a theoretical concept to a technology that influences nearly every aspect of modern life. From recommendation algorithms on social media to autonomous vehicles and medical diagnosis systems, AI systems are making decisions that affect billions of people daily. As these systems become more powerful and pervasive, questions about their ethical implications have moved from academic philosophy departments to the forefront of public debate.

B One of the most pressing ethical concerns surrounding AI is algorithmic bias. AI systems learn from historical data, and if that data reflects existing social inequalities, the AI will perpetuate and potentially amplify those inequalities. Studies have shown that facial recognition systems perform significantly worse on women and people with darker skin tones, that AI recruitment tools can discriminate against certain demographic groups, and that criminal justice algorithms may disproportionately flag minority individuals as high risk.

C The question of accountability when AI systems cause harm remains largely unresolved. When an autonomous vehicle causes an accident, who is responsible: the manufacturer, the software developer, or the vehicle owner? When an AI medical diagnosis system makes an error that leads to patient harm, who bears the legal and moral liability? These questions are becoming increasingly urgent as AI systems are deployed in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, criminal justice, and military operations.

D Efforts to address AI ethics are underway at multiple levels. Major technology companies have established ethics boards and published principles for responsible AI development. Governments around the world are developing regulatory frameworks for AI, with the European Union leading the way with its comprehensive AI Act. Academic researchers continue to develop technical solutions to problems such as algorithmic bias.
